principles: Mirror the upstream Authority contract instead of creating a parallel one.
Keep the CLI fail-closed when gate-capable input is missing or stale.
Keep docs, code, and smoke checks aligned on the same vocabulary.
Prefer the smallest downstream mirror that removes the bad label.
drivers: The Authority server story owns the server-side contract change.
The CLI still advertises mac_ui in code and docs.
The CLI must not add a new environment model just to clean up wording.

options.name: A: Mirror the upstream contract in CLI code and docs, preserving fail-closed behavior
pros: Keeps the CLI and Authority server vocabulary aligned.
Fixes the stale mac_ui wording in runtime and docs.
Avoids inventing a new local policy or environment tier.
cons: Touches both code and docs in one pass.

options.name: B: Only rewrite the visible failure strings and docs
cons: Leaves the live role check unchanged.
Lets code and docs disagree about gate actors.
Does not actually mirror the upstream contract.

options.name: C: Add a shared cross-repo role registry
pros: Creates a single shared vocabulary source.
cons: Much larger than needed for this fix.
Introduces a new coordination layer that is not required for the current correctness issue.

chosen: A: Mirror the upstream contract in CLI code and docs, preserving fail-closed behavior
rationale: Option A is the smallest coherent downstream fix: it removes the stale mac_ui label, keeps the CLI aligned with the upstream Authority contract, and does not invent a new policy or environment layer.

preMortem.scenario: The CLI still mentions mac_ui in one code path after the change.
preMortem.trigger: authority-client.ts and command-policy.ts are not updated together.
preMortem.consequence: The downstream contract stays inconsistent and the stale role remains visible.
preMortem.mitigation: Update both files in the same story and add smoke assertions that search for the removed wording.

preMortem.scenario: Docs drift from the updated CLI behavior.
preMortem.trigger: The decision docs are edited without matching the runtime role helper.
preMortem.consequence: Readers and tests see different gate vocabularies.
preMortem.mitigation: Search the docs for stale role names and keep the smoke/CLI code aligned with the docs pass.

preMortem.scenario: A cleanup accidentally widens the role set.
preMortem.trigger: The gate helper is refactored too aggressively while removing the label.
preMortem.consequence: The CLI would accept input that should still fail closed.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep explicit negative tests for missing or stale gate-capable input and verify no new environment tiers appear.
